name: Wingspan

source.title: Wingspan rulebook, university-hosted copy of the publisher file

setup.text: Shuffle the bird cards and turn 3 face up in the bird tray.
Put all food and egg tokens in the supply.
Roll the 5 food dice into the birdfeeder.
Choose a side of the goal board. Green is the default; blue gives 1 point per item and is suggested for new players.
Shuffle the goal tiles and put one on each round space of the goal board.
Take a player mat, 8 action cubes in one colour, 2 random bonus cards, 5 random bird cards and 5 food tokens, one of each type.
Keep up to 5 bird cards. Discard 1 food token for each bird you keep.
Keep 1 bonus card and discard the other. You may look at your bonus cards while choosing birds.
Pick the first player at random.

turn.summary: Place one action cube and take one of four actions.
steps: Play a bird: pay its food and egg cost and place it on your mat. Only its 'when played' power triggers.
Gain food, lay eggs or draw bird cards: put the cube on the leftmost open slot of that row and take what it shows.
Then activate the brown powers in that row from right to left. Each one is optional.

round_end: Remove your action cubes from your mat.
Score the round's goal, marking your result with one cube. That cube stays, which is why you have one fewer turn each round.
Discard the face-up birds in the tray and deal 3 new ones.
Pass the first player token clockwise.

scoring.text: Points printed on your bird cards.
1 point for each egg, each cached food token and each tucked card.

missed.text: If every die in the birdfeeder tray shows the same face, including when only one die is left, you may reroll all five before taking food.
If the birdfeeder tray is empty, roll all five dice back in.

not_covered: Solo play uses the separate Automa rulebook.
unverified: The three 1-point items in final scoring (eggs, cached food, tucked cards) are printed as icons in the rulebook and were confirmed from a rules summary, not the rulebook text.
Goal tile placement is summarised from a sentence that was cut off in the extracted text.
This file is an early printing; the publisher says later printings corrected some wording.
